**SECTION 1: TOPIC INTRODUCTION & DATABASE ARCHITECTURE**

**1.1 Management Problem Overview & System Scope**

In modern university academic administrations, manual processing of curriculum configurations, class section scheduling, student quota allocations, and matrix-based grading poses severe vulnerabilities. Errors commonly occur when prerequisite courses are overlooked, class capacities deviate from institutional targets, or component grading weights fail to sum to 100%.

The Student Mark Management System (SMMS) is engineered to solve these challenges through an automated, data-driven architecture. Built on ASP.NET Core 8 Web API and ASP.NET Core 8 MVC Razor Views, SMMS centralizes the complete academic lifecycle from curriculum versioning and automated class creation to strict prerequisite validation, 28–31 student class quota enforcement, real-time matrix grading, credit-weighted GPA calculation, audited administrative class transfers, and comprehensive semester closure checklists.

**1.2 Core CRUD Functions & System Capabilities**

**Functional Overview:** The system provides complete CRUD operations across all fundamental academic and administrative entities:

• Majors & Specializations: Management of major codes (SE, IA, AI, DS), descriptions, and branched specializations (SE-IS, SE-JS, SE-ES).

• Subjects & Dynamic Grade Components: Cataloging of course codes, credit values, descriptions, and dynamic grade components (Quiz, Lab, Assignment, FE) strictly validating that weight sums equal 100%.

• Prerequisite Course Management: Explicit prerequisite mapping enforcing a minimum score of 5.0/10 before students can enroll in advanced subjects.

• Curriculum Configurations: Flexible curriculum versioning by Major, Semester Number (1–9), and Specialization (mandatory from Semester 5+ for branching majors).

• Administrative Classes: Managing cohort-based homeroom groups (e.g., SE1701) with enrollment tracking.

• Course Sections: Managing operational semester sections with teacher assignment, classroom, schedule slots, capacity limits, and grade lock states.

**1.3 Authentication, Profile Management & Security Hardening**

**Security Architecture:** Security is implemented at both architectural and communication layers:

• JWT Bearer Authentication: Stateless token-based security containing user identification, role claims (Admin, Lecturer, Student), and student/lecturer foreign keys.

• BCrypt Password Encryption: Industry-standard adaptive salt hashing protecting credential stores against brute-force and rainbow table attacks.

• Soft Deletion & Account State (IsActive): Accounts are marked inactive rather than hard-deleted, permanently preserving historic transcripts and audit logs.

• User Profile Management: Dedicated \`/Account/Profile\` endpoint allowing users to view details, update contact records, and execute secure password changes.

**1.4 Import/Export, Advanced Search, Sorting & OData Integration**

**Data Interoperability:** To satisfy high-volume query and reporting demands, SMMS incorporates advanced data retrieval and interchange protocols:

• OData v4 Integration: The backend exposes OData endpoints under \`/odata/\` supporting \`\$filter\`, \`\$select\`, \`\$orderby\`, \`\$count\`, and \`\$search\` parameters for Subjects, Majors, and CourseSections.

• Advanced Multi-field Sorting: Sorting by course code, name, credits ascending/descending, and composite order-by sequences.

• Excel/CSV Export with UTF-8 BOM: Direct export of campus GPA rankings and section grade sheets into CSV format equipped with UTF-8 Byte Order Mark, ensuring flawless Vietnamese character display in Microsoft Excel.

• Microsoft Word (.docx) Reporting: Automated export generating formatted Word documents for institutional archiving.

**1.5 Database Design & Connection Architecture**

The relational database SMMS\_PRN232 is designed with 21 relational tables in Third Normal Form (3NF). The system connection is configured via \`AppDbContext\` using Microsoft SQL Server with automatic retry-on-failure capabilities.

![][image1]

*Figure 1: SMMS N-Tier System Architecture (Client, API, Business Services, Database)*

**1.5.1 Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) Specification**

The database design enforces relational integrity through primary keys, foreign keys with appropriate cascade/restrict behaviors, and composite unique constraints preventing duplicate enrollments or overlapping schedules.

![][image2]

*Figure 2: Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) with Core Relational Schemas & Cardinality*

**Table 4: Database Entity Classification (Strong vs. Weak Entities)**

| Classification | Entity Name | Primary Identifier | Relational Dependencies & Business Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Strong Entity | Users | Id (int, PK) | Independent identity storing credentials and system roles. |
| Strong Entity | Majors | Id (int, PK) | Master academic major catalog (e.g., SE, IA, AI). |
| Strong Entity | Subjects | Id (int, PK) | Course catalog storing code, name, and credit units. |
| Strong Entity | Semesters | Id (int, PK) | Academic calendar storing start/end and deadline dates. |
| Weak Entity | Specializations | Id (int, PK) | Dependent on Majors via MajorId foreign key. |
| Weak Entity | SubjectGradeComponents | Id (int, PK) | Dependent on Subjects via SubjectId foreign key. |
| Weak Entity | CourseSections | Id (int, PK) | Dependent on Semesters and Subjects. |
| Associative Entity | CourseSectionStudents | Composite (SectionId, StudentId) | Resolves M:N enrollment relationship with status. |

**1.5.2 Mapping Process from ERD to Relational Database Schema**

**Conversion Methodology:** The conversion from logical ERD to physical SQL Server schema adheres to formal database engineering rules:

1\. Regular (Strong) Entity Mapping: Each strong entity becomes a relation with its primary key defined as an Identity column (INT, NOT NULL, PK).

2\. One-to-One (1:1) Relationships: Mapped by placing a unique foreign key in the child table. For instance, \`Students.UserId\` is a unique foreign key referencing \`Users.Id\` with \`ON DELETE CASCADE\`.

3\. One-to-Many (1:N) Relationships: Mapped by inserting the parent's primary key into the child table as a foreign key. For example, \`Specializations.MajorId\` references \`Majors.Id\`, and \`CourseSections.SemesterId\` references \`Semesters.Id\`.

4\. Many-to-Many (M:N) Relationships: Resolved using intermediate associative tables equipped with composite primary keys. For instance, \`CourseSectionStudents\` resolves sections and students; \`PrerequisiteSubjects\` resolves subjects and prerequisite requirements.

5\. Integrity & Non-Nullability: Mandatory attributes are enforced as \`NOT NULL\`, while optional values (such as \`SpecializationId\` before semester 5 or \`Description\`) allow \`NULL\`.

**SECTION 2: DETAILED API SPECIFICATIONS & FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE**

**2.1 Detailed RESTful & OData Web API Specifications**

The Backend exposes 17 controllers delivering comprehensive RESTful endpoints and OData query support. All sensitive endpoints enforce JWT Bearer Authorization via \`\[Authorize(Policy \= ...)\]\`.

**Table 7: Comprehensive Web API Endpoints Specification**

| Resource Controller | HTTP Method | Endpoint Route | Parameters / Body | Return Type & Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AuthController | POST | /api/auth/login | LoginRequest {Username, Password} | LoginResponse (Token, UserInfo, Role) |
| AuthController | GET | /api/auth/me | Header: Authorization Bearer | UserDto (Current authenticated profile) |
| AuthController | PUT | /api/auth/profile | UpdateProfileRequest (Email, Phone, Pwd) | ApiResponse\<UserDto\> (Updated user) |
| UsersController | PATCH | /api/users/{id}/toggle-status | id (int), isActive (bool) | ApiResponse (Updated account state) |
| MajorsController | GET | /api/majors | None | List\<MajorDto\> with Specializations |
| SubjectsController | POST | /api/subjects/{id}/components | List\<CreateGradeComponentDto\> | ApiResponse (Enforces weight sum \== 100%) |
| CurriculumsController | GET | /api/curriculums/lookup | majorId, semesterNumber, specId | CurriculumLookupResponse with Subject list |
| AllocationsController | POST | /api/allocations/run | RunAllocationRequest {SemesterId} | AllocationResultDto (Batched quota engine) |
| CourseSectionsController | POST | /api/coursesections/{id}/assign-lecturer | AssignLecturerRequest {LecturerId} | ApiResponse (Immediate role transfer) |
| GradesController | GET | /api/grades/section/{id} | id (int) | SectionGradeSheetDto (Matrix grade sheet) |
| GradesController | POST | /api/grades/save | UpdateStudentGradeRequest {SectionId, Scores} | ApiResponse (Saves and calculates final score) |
| GradesController | POST | /api/grades/lock | LockGradeRequest {SectionId, IsLocked} | ApiResponse (Admin lock/unlock switch) |
| SemesterClosingController | GET | /api/semesterclosing/check/{semesterId} | semesterId (int) | SemesterClosingCheckResultDto (4 checks) |

**2.2 Frontend Application Architecture (ASP.NET Core 8 MVC)**

The Frontend is built as a responsive ASP.NET Core 8 MVC Web application running on Port 3000\. It communicates with the Backend Web API (Port 5050\) using a typed service \`ApiClientService\`.

![][image3]

*Figure 3: Authentication & JWT Claims Generation Sequence Flow*

**Client Networking Pipeline:** Key implementation details of \`ApiClientService.cs\`:

1\. Token Storage: Upon successful authentication via \`POST /api/auth/login\`, the JWT string is securely persisted in both \`HttpContext.Session\` ('SMMS\_JWT\_TOKEN') and an application cookie for client persistence.

2\. Bearer Header Injection: The private method \`CreateRequest(HttpMethod, endpoint)\` automatically retrieves the token and injects the header \`Authorization: Bearer \<token\>\` for all outgoing HTTP calls.

3\. Generic Serialization: \`GetAsync\<T\>\`, \`PostAsync\<T\>\`, \`PutAsync\`, and \`DeleteAsync\` deserialize API responses, supporting both custom \`ApiResponse\<T\>\` envelopes and OData v4 JSON payloads.

**2.3 Frontend Feature Highlights & UI Workflow Execution**

The user interface incorporates several UX optimizations to simplify complex administrative workflows:

• Compact 1-Dropdown Major Filter (\`/Majors\`): Replaced multi-row pills with a single full-option select dropdown. The page defaults cleanly to showing one focused major in full width, with zero flickering during server-side rendering.

• Real-Time Matrix Grading Sheet (\`/Grades/Index\`): Renders an interactive matrix with students as rows and grade components as columns. JavaScript dynamically recalculates weighted final scores on keyup.

![][image4]

*Figure 4: Automated Student Allocation Algorithm Flowchart (28-31 SV/class)*

• Allocation Batch Engine: As shown in Figure 4, students are verified against prerequisite courses (minimum score \>= 5.0) and assigned to sections adhering to the target 28–31 class size quota.

![][image5]

*Figure 5: Matrix Grading, 1-Decimal Rounding & Credit-Weighted GPA Computation Flow*

• Grading Logic & GPA Formulation: As illustrated in Figure 5, individual component scores are multiplied by component weights to compute the final score, rounded to 1 decimal place (e.g., 7.26 rounds to 7.3). Cumulative GPA on a 10-point scale is computed across all completed credits, explicitly factoring in failed courses.

![][image6]

*Figure 6: Semester Closing 4-Condition Checklist & Exception Override Flow*

• Semester Closure Checklist: As detailed in Figure 6, the system validates four critical prerequisites: unassigned teachers, unlocked grades, missing components, and unallocated students. If exceptions occur, Admin can perform an audited override with documented justification.

• Vietnamese Diacritics Preservation: \`DatabaseFontFixer.cs\` automatically resolves character encoding conflicts on seed records.

**SECTION 4: EVALUATION, LIMITATIONS & FUTURE ENHANCEMENTS**

**4.1 Technical Achievements & Architecture Strengths**

• Clean Separation of Concerns: Clear isolation between Presentation (Razor Views), Controller mediation, Application Services, and EF Core Data layers.

• High Query Performance: Elimination of N+1 query traps through pre-loaded configuration dictionaries and single-pass SQL GroupBy aggregations.

• Enterprise Data Integrity: Strict weight sum validation (100%), automated prerequisite screening, and asynchronous audit trails.

• Automated xUnit Test Coverage: 5 out of 5 core business validation unit tests in \`project\_PRN232.Tests\` execute with 100% pass rates.

**4.2 Known Limitations**

• Retake Courses (Học lại): Current scope does not automate retake grade replacement algorithms.

• Payment Gateway: Tuition fee accounting and credit-based billing are outside the current release scope.

• External SIS Integration: Synchronizing rosters with national student ID databases currently requires CSV batch imports.

**4.3 Future Development Roadmap**

• Real-Time Push Notifications: Integrating ASP.NET Core SignalR for real-time alerts when grades are unlocked or published.

• Mobile Companion App: Developing cross-platform mobile clients using .NET MAUI.

• AI Academic Advising: Incorporating machine learning models to detect at-risk students based on prerequisite performance patterns.
